### A1. Section 3.2 (existing collapse reaches exactly [0, R]) — **HOLDS as mathematics, DERIVED**

Claim: for fixed R ∈ [0,1], f(p) = R(1−p)/(1−pR) over p ∈ [0,1] has range exactly [0, R].

Derivation: denominator 1−pR ≥ 1−R ≥ 0, and = 0 only if p = R = 1, where f has limit 0. Elsewhere f ≥ 0 (numerator, denominator non-negative). f ≤ R ⟺ R(1−p) ≤ R(1−pR) ⟺ (for R > 0) 1−p ≤ 1−pR ⟺ pR ≤ p, true since R ≤ 1; R = 0 gives f ≡ 0. Endpoints: f(0) = R, f(1) = 0. Continuity plus monotonicity (df/dp = −R(1−R)/(1−pR)² ≤ 0) gives the full interval. **The upper bound R is the load-bearing fact and it is exact: a review-only pass can never increase residual risk in this model.**

### A3. Section 3.4 (flat curve hides R\* = b/p) — **HOLDS as mathematics, with one scope note, DERIVED**

Take the fault-count recursion behind the risk form: N_{k+1} = N_k(1−p) + b′, with b′ the per-round injected fault count and p the sensitivity. Fixed point N\* = b′/p. Per-round discoveries = pN_k → pN\* = b′. **Scope note — and this is the one place CC1's statement is loose:** CC1 writes "in every case the per-round discovery rate decays to essentially 0." Discoveries decay to **b′**, not to 0; they decay *to* 0 only when b′ = 0. What CC1's numbers actually show is the sharper, correct point: discoveries **converge to a constant b′** (b = 0.02, p = 0.35 ⇒ 2% of fault mass surfaced per round, forever), and a discovery rate that is *flat at a small constant* is **indistinguishable from convergence-to-zero at any realistic noise floor and round count**. At b = 0.02 the steady-state surface rate is ~2 findings per 100 faults per round — below any plausible new-critical threshold and visually flat within a few rounds (transient decays geometrically at factor 1−p = 0.65: after 5 rounds the transient is 0.65⁵ ≈ 11.6% of its start). So the hole is real: **the discovery curve cannot separate "nothing left" from "steady-state churn at b/p" once b′ is small.** The numerical trio (5.71%, 28.57%, 57.14% at p = 0.35) is just b/p: 0.02/0.35, 0.10/0.35, 0.20/0.35 ✓. Verdict: HOLDS, with "decays to 0" corrected to "decays to b′, which presents as ~0."

### A4. Does the two-sided gate close the hole? (Question 3) — **PARTIAL: closes it only under a condition the revision's own parameterisation can violate. DERIVED construction**

The gate (per CC1's 3.5, executed on the real `_check_gamma_alt_convergence` — I could not re-execute) fires on new criticals. Construct the failure case concretely:

Let the original defect population have critical-fraction ρ₀ = 0.4, review sensitivity p = 0.35 to it. Let repairs inject defects at rate b with critical-fraction ρ₁ and sensitivity p₁. Steady-state *critical* surfacing rate ≈ b·ρ₁·(visibility factor). The gate's critical-side stays silent iff b·ρ₁ is below the gate's "new critical" threshold θ — i.e. iff **ρ₁ < θ/b**. With θ = 1 critical/round (CC1: "even 1 new critical in the last round refuses") and b = 0.05 fault-mass/round over a 200-fault artefact, injections stay sub-critical iff they average fewer than 1 critical per round — i.e. a repair regime that injects *many low-severity defects and a critical only every few rounds* sits at residual risk b/p = 14.3% while the gate's critical side sees 0 most rounds and the gamma side sees a flat, quiet curve.

The gate fires only if ρ₁·b ≥ 1 critical in the *last* round (or A4-unresolved accumulates). Two structural gaps, both derivable without the repo:

1. **Sensitivity asymmetry (the brief's own case).** If injected defects belong to a class the same review is less sensitive to (p₁ < p), the recursion for that class settles at N₁\* = b₁/p₁ — *higher* residual than b₁/p₀ — while its surfacing rate p₁N₁\* = b₁ is *the same*. The gate reads surfacing; residual grows as sensitivity drops. **A repair that injects defects the panel is bad at seeing raises true residual risk with zero change in anything the gate observes.** This is not a calibration quibble; it is the formal statement that a surfacing-based gate has a blindness exactly where repair quality and review capability are correlated — and in this project they are correlated, because the same models write the repairs and run the review.

2. **Severity drift.** Gate critical-side triggers on *criticals*. A repair regime that trades one critical for ten majors lowers the gate's trigger rate while raising total residual risk mass. Under §10 materiality, ten majors that ship may or may not clear θ_crit — but the *gate* as described counts criticals.

So: **the two-sided gate closes the b/p hole iff injected defects surface as criticals at a rate the critical-side threshold catches within the round window.** The revision's (s, b) parameterisation is precisely what is needed to *state* this condition. Whether the project *needs* to state it is Part C. Verdict on CC1's 3.5: PARTIAL — true for the regime CC1 tested (injected defects = new criticals), not true in general; the test suite exercised the gate against the friendly case.
